mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a single month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases > 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO declines > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increases > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% each over three months signals strong demand in both housing and consumer sectors, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each over 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where the level of the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 2%.
